title: Beni Mellal city and foothills, 16 Jul to 14 Sep 2026
summary: From 16 Jul to 14 Sep 2026 the radar shows 2.81 km2 turning brighter in HV around Beni Mellal, against 1.48 km2 darker, mostly on the changing fields. HH turned brighter on 5.27 km2, and mean HH rose by 0.45 dB.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 60 days mean HV moved by 0.04 dB. In HV, 2.81 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 1.48 km2 darker; in HH, 5.27 km2 turned brighter and 1.08 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 1.95 km2 brighter and 0.91 km2 darker in HV, rising 0.83 dB, and 2.12 km2 brighter in HH. Rough dry ground and fields had 1.53 km2 brighter in HH, rising 0.86 dB, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 0.91 km2. Built-up land rose 0.39 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the brighter fields: new crops sown in late summer; sowing records or a field visit would confirm it. Possible cause for the brighter HH on rough ground: tillage that roughens the soil; the optical photo would show it. Possible cause for part of the HH rise: a small calibration difference between the acquisitions.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: A farm office could compare the 1.95 km2 of brighter fields with its sowing records. Treat HH changes under one dB as uncertain until stable targets confirm them.
